summary: Built in 1928 as a scenic viewing tower in Cook Forest State Park, it was later staffed as a fire lookout until a 1977 tornado knocked out its lines.

access.note: Tower open to visitors year-round; the cab itself opens only during interpretive programming.

facts.agency: Pennsylvania Department of Conservation and Natural Resources

events.note: Built as a scenic viewing attraction for park visitors, not originally a fire lookout
Began service as a paid state forest observer position
End of paid observer staffing; volunteers took over in 1967
Tornado destroyed the tower's phone and electric lines, ending volunteer watch duty
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, January 23, 2017

evidence.quote: This 87.5-foot steel tower was originally built as a tourist scenic viewing attraction in 1928.
It was manned as a paid forest observer position from 1946-1966.
Volunteers manned it from 1967 until a tornado took out its phone and electric lines in 1977.

evidence.supports: current public scenic use, cab open only during programming
evidence.quote: It currently functions as it was originally designed, for the public to take a scenic view of the area. Heavily visited during the summer season, often seeing 200-400 visitors every two hours. Although the tower is open to visitation year round, the cab is open only during interpretive programming.

evidence.supports: NHLR register number and registration date

corrections.why: NHLR describes an "87.5-foot steel tower", which converts to about 26.7 m, not the record's 24.4 m (80 ft).

notes_for_editor: Only the NHLR page yielded verifiable content within budget; the eastern_us_lookouts cached page for Cook Forest is a thin stub (nav index only, no body text) and the PA StoryMap/Wikidata/OSM sources already in the tower record were not independently re-verified. The 'design: Aermotor' and height_m=24.4 fields in the tower record come from pa_storymap and were not confirmed here; NHLR's stated 87.5 ft tower height conflicts with the record's 24.4 m (80 ft), flagged as a correction. Current staffing/operational status beyond 1977 is unknown from available sources.
